3/21/25, 10:27 AM - +353 83 822 4226: So, the heat pump heating system is designed to work constantly. Low temp but constantly. That's the way the heat pump uses less electricity cos it doesn't need to rise the temp from like 18 to 22 degrees in the house but from 22 to 23.
There is also less stress on the heat pump (external unit) with the immersion element that helps raising the temp when higher temp is needed (anti legionella programme). Basically, immersion helps the heat pump and it doesn't need to work as hard.
3/21/25, 10:28 AM - +353 83 822 4226: Hiya 
So, I went for a "slightly" oversized system of 15 panels, generating 6250 kWh a year. 
It completely eliminated my electricity bill and I do have some profit from it.
It would be the best to see how much your household consumes on yearly basis and then to see what size of the system would suit you. Like, if the household uses 5000 kWh a year, to cut your bill in half, you would need a system that generates 2500kWh, to reduce the bill by 70%, you would need system that generates 3500 kWh a year and so on.

Cost of my system (15 panels generating 6250 kWh a year) was 8.5k.

I will forward you the number, the man's name is Paddy.
In the price is included recertification of BER.
With my system, I got A1 BER cert (tho I think I should be rated as a passive house as the calculation is that the house is using minus 22 kWh per square meter per year 😂)

7/29/25, 2:15 PM - +353 85 121 9306: The light fixture in the image is likely an integrated LED panel or downlight, such as the V-TAC Panel LED Wpuszczany Premium Downlight, which means it does not have a traditional removable "bulb" that can be changed. Instead, the LED components are built directly into the fixture. 
If the light source fails, the entire fixture typically needs to be replaced. To replace such a fixture: 
1. Turn off power:
Locate the circuit breaker controlling the light fixture and turn off the power to prevent electric shock.
2. Remove the old fixture:
Depending on the installation type (recessed or surface-mounted), this might involve carefully prying out the fixture from the ceiling or unscrewing it. For recessed panels, you might need to release retention springs.
3. Disconnect wiring:
Disconnect the electrical wiring, noting how the wires are connected (e.g., live, neutral, ground).
4. Install the new fixture:
Connect the new fixture's wiring to the corresponding house wiring, ensuring secure connections.
5. Secure the new fixture:
Install the new fixture into the ceiling or on the surface, ensuring it is properly secured.
6. Restore power:
Turn the power back on at the circuit breaker and test the new light.

9/21/25, 8:01 AM - +353 86 270 4385: 1. This is a slow heating system. It is much more energy efficient, but it takes up to a day to heat up 
2. Make sure all doors are properly closed (they explain in the manual how to do it) and windows 
3. The heather won't feel warm. And that is normal.
4. It is possible that you might need to remove the air for the heaters. That is not a big issue. You can ask the folks at Castlehorn to help! <This message was edited>

11/19/25, 11:25 AM - +353 89 438 8328: I have chat GPT the manual of my heat pump ( which should be the same you have) and asked about that code error. This is the answer:

Here’s the meaning of error code 002 on your Hitachi Yutaki S / Sigma controller — explained clearly and based on how the system behaves:

⸻

🔵 Error Code 002 – Low Water Pressure / Insufficient Water Flow

This code means the hydraulic (water) side of your heat pump does not have enough pressure or flow to operate safely.

It is not a refrigerant (gas) problem — it’s the water circuit.

⸻

✅ What Error 002 Usually Means
	1.	System water pressure is too low
	•	Often below 1.0 bar
	•	Heat pump cannot circulate enough water through radiators/underfloor loops.
	2.	Air is still trapped in the system
	•	Even if you bled some radiators, pockets of air in the pipes, pump, or hydrobox can stop flow and trigger 002.
	3.	Circulation pump issue
	•	Pump may be air-locked or temporarily stuck.
	4.	Flow switch or sensor triggered
	•	If flow is slow or interrupted, the system stops to protect the heat exchanger.

⸻

🔧 What You Should Do Now (Step-by-Step)

✔️ 1. Check your water pressure

Look at the pressure reading on the Sigma controller home screen (or the little gauge on the hydrobox if you have one).

You want:
	•	1.2 – 1.5 bar when cold
	•	Up to 2.0 bar when hot is normal

👉 If it shows below 1 bar, that will cause 002 immediately.

⸻

✔️ 2. Increase the pressure (if low)

Use the filling loop (silver braided hose with valves on each end) near your indoor unit.
	1.	Open the valve slowly
	2.	Watch the gauge rise
	3.	Stop at 1.4–1.6 bar

⚠️ Do not exceed 2 bar when cold.

⸻

✔️ 3. Bleed the radiators again

Important: if you added water, air will appear again.

Bleed:
	•	Highest radiators first
	•	Then the lower ones
	•	Top up to ~1.5 bar again if needed

⸻

✔️ 4. Reset the alarm

After fixing pressure/air:
	1.	Press Menu
	2.	Go to Alarms / Error list
	3.	Highlight “002”
	4.	Hold OK for 5 seconds to clear it

If the alarm doesn’t clear, you can also try:
	•	Turning the whole system off at the isolation switch
	•	Waiting 5 minutes
	•	Turning it back on

⸻

🔍 If the pressure is normal AND you bled the system, but 002 stays:

Then the issue is likely one of the following:
	•	Airlock inside the circulation pump
	•	Flow switch stuck
	•	Pump not running (electrical or mechanical)
	•	Blocked filter (common!) — inside the hydrobox there’s a small strainer

These require an engineer.

⸻

🧭 Quick summary

Code	Meaning	What to Check
002	Low water pressure / insufficient flow	Pressure 1–1.5 bar, bleed radiators, reset


⸻

If you want, tell me what pressure you see now on the controller, and I can guide you exactly through what to do next.

1/20/26, 4:03 PM - +353 89 483 4381: Yes — Revolut is generally considered safe to use for banking and holding money in Ireland, but there are a few important details to understand before you treat it exactly like a traditional Irish bank:  ￼

✅ 1. Licensed & Regulated as a Bank in the EU

Revolut Bank UAB holds a full banking licence issued by the European Central Bank (ECB) and regulated by the Bank of Lithuania. This licence allows it to operate across the EU, including in Ireland.  ￼

✅ 2. Deposit Protection Scheme

Because it’s a regulated bank, your eligible deposits are protected up to €100,000 per person under the Lithuanian Deposit Insurance Scheme, similar to how Irish banks are covered by the Irish Deposit Guarantee Scheme. In the very unlikely event Revolut Bank were to fail, this scheme is designed to compensate depositors up to that amount.  ￼

🔐 3. Security & Fraud Protection

Revolut uses modern security features like:
	•	Biometric login, strong authentication, and fraud monitoring
	•	Instant card freezing and alerts for suspicious transactions
These help protect your account from unauthorised access and fraud.  ￼

However, like all banks, you still need to practice good security habits: keep passwords secure, enable two-factor authentication, watch out for phishing scams, etc.  ￼

⚠️ 4. Irish Regulatory Role

While Revolut is regulated prudentially by Lithuania (ECB & Bank of Lithuania), it also operates in Ireland and must follow certain Irish conduct rules (e.g., consumer protections).  ￼

👍 5. Good for Everyday Banking & Payments

Revolut is widely used for everyday banking — receiving salary, making payments, and holding funds — and generally considered safe by financial commentators when used responsibly.  ￼

⚠️ 6. Some People Prefer a Traditional Bank for Large Balances

A few users prefer keeping larger savings or long-term savings in traditional Irish banks or splitting funds across banks, since deposit protection caps at €100,000. Having multiple banks can spread risk.  ￼

2/16/26, 1:49 PM - +353 83 822 4226: Just checked with Gemini and chat gpt
In the Hitachi Yutaki ecosystem, Alarm Code 002 is a high-pressure safety trip. It means the pressure in the refrigerant cycle has exceeded the safety limit, causing the system to shut down instantly to protect the compressor.
Hydraulic Blockage or Low Flow: This is the most common cause for an 8kW unit. 
The stagnant water in the heat exchanger overheats, causing the refrigerant pressure to skyrocket
Air in the System: If air is trapped in your new attic pipework or the main run, it can create an air lock that stops water flow.

4/18/26, 7:17 PM - +353 89 481 8582: Just checked the timelines online.
Once a formal complaint is logged with eir, they must acknowledge it within 2 working days and aim to provide a response or proposed resolution within 10 working days. If there’s no satisfactory resolution after those 10 working days, you can escalate it to ComReg (Ireland’s communications regulator).

In my own complaint, I clearly stated that I wanted the issue fixed asap, or the option to exit the contract without early cancellation charges. They replied the next day and offered “end of next week” as the target date — otherwise, they said I could break the contract penalty-free.
Sharing in case it helps you or anyone in a similar situation! 🙂

7/17/26, 10:51 PM - Jayakumar Ballymakenny: This point is partly correct, but it depends on who owns the playground.
If the playground is on privately owned land within a residential estate, it is not the same as a public park. Many Irish housing estates have playgrounds and communal areas that are owned by the Management Company for the benefit of residents. In those cases, the Management Company can make rules restricting use to residents and their guests, and can erect signs stating this.
If, however, the playground has been taken in charge by the local authority (Louth County Council) and is a public amenity, then it is generally open to everyone, and the Management Company cannot exclude members of the public.

7/24/26, 10:27 PM - +353 89 985 1533: Hi everyone, just wanted to share this in case it helps anyone in the future.

I recently had an issue with the Calpeda attic booster pump where it was short cycling (starting and stopping on its own) and there was also water leaking around the tank/pump.

It took me over a month of going back and forth between Calpeda, Castlethorn, and Larkfield Plumbing before it was finally resolved.

Initially, Calpeda declined the warranty claim, stating the pump was over two years old based on its manufacturing date which was in early 2024. However, as the house itself was only handed over in December 2024, I escalated the matter with Castlethorn, who coordinated everything and got the issue resolved.

If anyone experiences a similar problem:

* Don’t assume it’s out of warranty because of the pump’s manufacturing date.
* Contact Castlethorn and ask them to coordinate with the plumbing contractor.
* Keep photos/videos of the issue and be persistent if you’re being passed between different companies.

Hopefully this saves someone else the time and frustration I went through. Feel free to message me if you ever need the contact details.  😊

8/17/26, 1:11 PM - Jayakumar Ballymakenny: Dear Lauren and Aftersales,

I am writing to raise a serious concern regarding the heavy vibration and noise experienced in the estate today, which we believe may be related to the piling/groundworks currently taking place at the rear of the estate for the construction of the new houses.

The vibration was extremely strong and continued for a considerable period. It was not just noticeable but was strong enough to cause items inside our homes to shake. For example, my TV almost fell from its stand, while doors and the fridge were visibly rattling/battering during the works.

Naturally, residents are now very concerned about whether these repeated and significant vibrations could have any impact on the structural integrity of the houses that have already been built and are currently occupied.

We would therefore ask the developer and the construction/engineering team to urgently investigate this matter and provide residents with reassurance, including details of the measures being taken to monitor and prevent any potential damage to the existing properties.

Given the intensity of today's vibration and noise, we would also strongly request that the construction team consider alternative construction methods to piling, or at the very least adopt appropriate measures to significantly reduce the vibration and noise affecting the existing homes.

We would appreciate an urgent response confirming:

- What construction activity caused today's level of vibration and noise.
- Whether vibration monitoring is being carried out and what the recorded levels were.
- What assessment has been made regarding the potential impact on the existing houses.
- What alternative methods or mitigation measures can be considered to reduce the vibration.
- How residents will be protected from potential damage while the construction works continue.

This is a serious concern for residents, and we would appreciate this being treated as an urgent health, safety and property-protection matter, rather than simply as a noise complaint.

I look forward to your prompt response and to seeing appropriate action taken before further piling or similar high-vibration works continue.

Kind regards,

Jay Nair
